title: STRANGE MINUTE #22

lines.text: You've never seen Venus this bright. Look up this week.
Before sunrise, look east. That blazing 'star' is a planet.
Around November 29th, it shines its brightest of the year.
lines.say: Around November twenty-ninth, it shines its brightest of the year.

lines.text: Only the Moon outshines it in the night sky.
But up close, Venus might be the worst place in the solar system.
The ground is about 870 degrees. Hot enough to melt lead.
lines.say: The ground is about eight hundred seventy degrees. Hot enough to melt lead.

lines.text: The air is so heavy, it's like being 3,000 feet underwater.
lines.say: The air is so heavy, it's like being three thousand feet underwater.

lines.text: A day on Venus is longer than its whole year.
It even spins backwards, so the Sun rises in the west.
The toughest probe that landed there lasted about two hours.
So, will you set an alarm to catch it?

sources: ScienceDaily (Nov 2026 sky guide): Venus at peak brightness Nov 29 (morning sky after Oct inferior conjunction)
NASA Venus facts: surface ~465 °C / 870 °F (lead melts 621 °F); pressure ~90× Earth ≈ 900 m / 3,000 ft underwater; sulfuric-acid clouds
NASA: rotation 243 Earth days > orbit 225 days; retrograde rotation (Sun rises in the west)
Venera 13 (1982) survived ~127 minutes on the surface
